Soft-tissue injury: 1

A patient receives a blunt blow to the thigh and develops tenderness with diffuse bruising. The skin remains closed and there is no discrete fluid collection. Which general soft-tissue injury term best describes this damage?

  1. Fracture blister
  2. Threatened skin from tenting
  3. Degloving injury
  4. Contusion
  5. Hematoma
Answer and explanation

Contusion

Blunt trauma can damage tissue and small vessels without a discrete skin opening.

Option explanations

Contusion: Blunt trauma can damage tissue and small vessels without a discrete skin opening.

Hematoma: A localized collection of blood differs from diffuse edema. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Fracture blister: Severe swelling can separate skin layers and produce blisters over an injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Threatened skin from tenting: A sharp displaced fragment may compromise overlying skin and requires urgent reassessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Degloving injury: Skin and subcutaneous tissue separate from deeper fascia, potentially disrupting perfusion even when the skin initially appears intact. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
